correctness.rationale: For any interior threshold, direct integration gives edge variance v and common-endpoint edge covariance c, with all disjoint edges independent; the unsigned incidence calculation yields Cov(Y)=(v-2c)Q+cQ². Exact piecewise integration gives c=r³(4-3r)/12 and a=v-2c=r²(3r²-8r+6)/12, both positive. Strict monotonicity on the positive spectrum gives the principal-square-root inverse and the precise bipartite-kernel statement. The matrix-square-root Sylvester bound and Hoeffding union bound justify the stated conservative sample requirement; no conditional independence between degrees is assumed. Packaged checker passed 11215 finite checks including all labelled hosts through five vertices. Finite tests alone are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The natural question of identifying a hidden host from only repeated sampled degree vectors is completely resolved, for all labelled finite simple hosts and every nondegenerate threshold. The quadratic signless-Laplacian covariance law is an exact observable-to-structure bridge in a model with dependent edges; it supplies a constructive inverse, a finite-sample guarantee, and a bipartite-component diagnostic. The known independent-percolation linear analog is acknowledged, while the dependent-edge formula and all-threshold classification are not merely a finite table or a substitution in a previously stated result. The bounds are deliberately not represented as minimax optimal.
